name: Death in the Afternoon
description: Absinthe topped with cold sparkling wine until it turns cloudy. Two ingredients; needs absinthe.
history: Ernest Hemingway contributed it to the 1935 celebrity cocktail book So Red the Nose, naming it after his 1932 book on bullfighting. His instructions: pour one jigger of absinthe into a champagne glass and add iced champagne until it reaches the proper opalescent milkiness. Drink three to five slowly.
whyItWorks: Sparkling wine louches the absinthe the way water does, so the drink turns milky green and the anise softens.

ingredients.label: Champagne or dry sparkling wine, very cold

steps: Pour the absinthe into a chilled coupe or flute.
Top slowly with very cold sparkling wine until the drink turns cloudy.
techniqueNotes: Hemingway’s jigger was a full 1.5 oz. One ounce is plenty for most people.
Brut Champagne or a dry cava works better than a sweet prosecco.
creator: Ernest Hemingway
